root_cause: The ReprHighlighter 'url' regex character class [-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]* did not include '@', so URLs such as https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips stopped matching at the '@' and only the prefix was highlighted as repr.url.
best_solution: Add '@' to the allowed-character class of the url pattern in ReprHighlighter.highlights (rich/highlighter.py): (?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*). The statement says literally 'Added @ in rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern', so the fix is a one-character regex edit; '@' is a valid URL char (userinfo and path segments), and extending the class lets the greedy match run to the end of the URL.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_highlighter.py parametrized highlight_tests gains ("https://www.youtube.com/@LinusTechTips", [Span(0, 38, "repr.url")]) inserted after the '#anchor' case at line ~136; test_highlight_regex must produce exactly one repr.url span covering the whole string. Any position of '@' inside the class passes.
locating_signals: Statement names the exact location: 'rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern' and the test file test_highlighter. The linked issue title '@ breaks highlighting in hyperlinks' plus grepping '(?P<url>' finds the single line.
our_outcome_summary: Only v8 passed (58s, 33 calls): identical source edit to gold, plus a stray reproduce_issue.py (harmless). v4 failed with empty patch: ContextWindowExceededError at 32768 tokens after 10 tool calls/321s, never edited. v6 had the byte-identical gold source edit but ALSO added its own test row to tests/test_highlighter.py at line 137, exactly where the hidden test_patch inserts; git apply of test_patch failed ('patch failed: tests/test_highlighter.py:134'), so the run scored as unresolved despite a correct fix. v7 put '@' in the class but left a trailing double comma ('...]*)",,') making rich/highlighter.py a SyntaxError on import; it also edited the test file (different hunk).
generalizable_lesson: Do not edit existing test files that the hidden test patch is likely to touch (especially inserting rows into a parametrized list next to the case the PR describes); hidden test patches are applied with git apply after your diff, and a context conflict voids a correct fix. Put any repro in a scratch file or revert test edits before finishing. Also re-run an import/py_compile of every edited source file after a one-line regex edit to catch stray punctuation like a double comma.
acceptable_alternatives: Placing '@' anywhere inside the character class (e.g. after '!' as v7 did) is equivalent; any broader URL class that includes '@' and still yields a single span for the other existing URL test cases would pass.
